title: bug: VS Code protected seat launch resolves the wrapper's interpreter by name (win32 shellPath 'powershell.exe' plus a typed `powershell`; POSIX a typed `bash`) with cwd = the workspace (VS Code twin of task-b071e3bf)
description:
Found in the 2026-11-03 client hunt (governor msg-33787f69). This is the VS Code parity twin of task-b071e3bf; JetBrains goes first, so this row depends on it.

Under protected (AgentLauncher.ts:351: `runtimeProfile(workspacePath) === 'protected' || vmSeat`), resolved.envOverrides carry MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 (:125) plus the installed daemon and proxy paths. The interpreter that runs the installed wrapper is still chosen by name:
- win32: WINDOWS_SHELL = 'powershell.exe' (:30) is passed as createTerminal({ cwd: workspacePath, shellPath: WINDOWS_SHELL }) (:411-415). A bare shellPath is resolved through PATH, with relative entries joined to the cwd, and then falls back to <cwd>\powershell.exe. Inside that shell the typed line (:287) starts `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -EncodedCommand ...`, which is another lookup by name on PATH.
- POSIX: buildBashCommand (:307) types `<env> bash '<script>' --role ...` into the default profile shell with cwd = the workspace. So a '.', empty, relative or in-project PATH entry reaches <workspace>/bash, the task-0d9ebe5b repro shape.

Fix: apply the rule task-b071e3bf settles for JetBrains. Under protected only, use an absolute interpreter outside the workspace, both for shellPath and for the typed first word; a missing interpreter refuses before createTerminal. Legacy lines stay byte-identical. Read mem:gotcha-vscode-tests-need-full-repo-snapshot before planning the gate. Docs belong to the epic final task (task-f3f364a6).
definitionOfDone: Under protected, the VS Code launch starts the wrapper's interpreter by an absolute path outside the workspace: the win32 shellPath, the typed PowerShell line and the POSIX bash line. No PATH or current-directory lookup can select a workspace file, and a missing interpreter refuses before any terminal is created.
Legacy launch lines and the legacy terminal options are byte-identical to today's, and the existing moe-vscode launcher tests stay green unchanged.

New moe-vscode tests pin the protected interpreter on both platforms and fail on today's bytes (RED recorded). `npm test && npm run compile` for moe-vscode is green in a snapshot run, per the live-runtime rail.

implementationPlan.description:
Tests first (load test-driven-development). This row mirrors task-b071e3bf: JetBrains goes first, and this row dependsOn it. Read its landed plan and code before starting. If it settled a different interpreter or check, mirror that instead, and say so in complete_step.

The rule applies under protected only (runtimeProfile(...) === 'protected' || vmSeat). The wrapper's interpreter is an absolute path outside the workspace, chosen by a new export in moe-vscode/src/util/AgentLauncher.ts: `protectedInterpreter(basePath, windows = process.platform === 'win32', env = process.env, posixBash = '/bin/bash')`.
- POSIX: posixBash, which is moe-agent.sh's own shebang.
- win32: path.win32.join(env.SystemRoot, 'System32', 'WindowsPowerShell', 'v1.0', 'powershell.exe').
- Both go through MoeDaemonClient.installedExecutable with a label (step 2). The POSIX label is `wrapper interpreter ${posixBash}`; the win32 label is the fixed text 'wrapper interpreter %SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe'. The result is { accepted: <real path> } or { rejected: <reason> }.

The protected typed line starts with that real path:
- POSIX: `<env> '<interp>' '<wrapper>' --role ...`.
- win32: `<env>& '<interp>' -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -EncodedCommand <b64>`. The win32 terminal's shellPath is the same path.

A rejection shows `Protected execution profile: <reason>. Moe starts the agent wrapper only with an interpreter outside the project.` and creates no terminal. Legacy is unchanged: the typed `bash` and `powershell`, the win32 shellPath 'powershell.exe', and every legacy row.

Rows in moe-vscode/tests/protected-runtime.test.cjs (reuse its harness; tests share no helper module):
- interp() gives the expected real path: fs.realpathSync.native('/bin/bash'), or on win32 fs.realpathSync.native(path.join(process.env.SystemRoot, 'System32', 'WindowsPowerShell', 'v1.0', 'powershell.exe')).
- L1 already exists. It pins the PROTECTED line, which DoD 1 changes. expectedCommand gains an optional interpreter argument, and L1 expects the interpreter form. L1 also asserts the terminal options: on win32 {name: 'Moe Coder', cwd: dir, shellPath: interp()}; elsewhere, no shellPath key. L4 (legacy) passes no interpreter and stays byte-identical.
- L5 tests protectedInterpreter in one table; each row is skipped off its platform.
  - POSIX: the defaults give { accepted: interp() }. posixBash '/nonexistent/bash' gives { rejected: 'wrapper interpreter /nonexistent/bash not found' }. posixBash 'bash' gives '... is not an absolute path'. posixBash set to a file written inside the project gives '... resolves inside the project'.
  - win32: env { SystemRoot: process.env.SystemRoot } gives { accepted: interp() }. env {} gives '... not found'. { SystemRoot: 'Windows' } gives '... is not an absolute path'. { SystemRoot: <a temp dir outside the project with no powershell.exe> } gives '... not found'. { SystemRoot: <the project dir> }, with System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe written inside it, gives '... resolves inside the project'.
- L6: a protected launch (declare('verified-local') plus extension()). The client stub's installedExecutable returns { rejected: 'wrapper interpreter X not found' } and counts its calls.
  - errors === ['Protected execution profile: wrapper interpreter X not found. Moe starts the agent wrapper only with an interpreter outside the project.'];
  - no terminal is created, and the stub was called once;
  - under a legacy launch (project(undefined, true)) the same stub gets zero calls, and L4's line is unchanged.

In moe-vscode/tests/verified-local-launch.test.cjs, expectedCommand's marker rows (V2 for architect and governor, V4 for worker and QA: the protected runtime) expect the interpreter form. Marker-false rows stay byte-identical.

These are the only existing rows that change, because they pin exactly the protected line that DoD 1 changes. Record that reading of DoD 2 in complete_step.

Run both files RED in a Linux snapshot (step 4's archive, overlay and npm ci, then `node --test tests/protected-runtime.test.cjs tests/verified-local-launch.test.cjs`). L1, V2, V4, L5 and L6 must fail on today's bytes, and the legacy rows must pass. Keep that tail: it is the RED that DoD 3 asks for.

Error handling in the tests: every temp dir goes into the existing `made` cleanup, and no row depends on PATH.

implementationPlan.description:
Implementation in moe-vscode/src/util/AgentLauncher.ts:
- Import installedExecutable and defaultFoldCase (and the ArtifactSelection type) from '../services/MoeDaemonClient'.
- Add the exported protectedInterpreter(...) from step 1, with a doc comment naming task-d5eca150 and its JetBrains twin.
- In launchRole, compute `const protectedRun = runtimeProfile(workspacePath) === 'protected' || vmSeat;` once and choose `resolved` from it. runtimeProfile still runs first, exactly as today, because it pins.
- After the existing refusal and not-found checks, when protectedRun: `const selection = protectedInterpreter(workspacePath)`. A rejection shows step 1's message and returns, before the readiness await and before createTerminal. Otherwise interpreter = selection.accepted.
- buildPowerShellCommand and buildBashCommand take an optional last `interpreter`, and assertSafeLaunchArgs checks it for control characters when it is set.
  - PowerShell: `${prefix}${interpreter ? `& ${psQuote(interpreter)}` : 'powershell'} -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -EncodedCommand ${encoded}`.
  - Bash: `${prefix}${interpreter ? shQuote(interpreter) : 'bash'} ${shQuote(scriptPath)} ...`.
- createTerminal: `...(isWin ? { shellPath: interpreter ?? WINDOWS_SHELL } : {})`. POSIX options stay {name, cwd}, so the user's profile shell still sets PATH for node and claude.

Error handling: protectedInterpreter never throws, because installedExecutable maps every fs error to a reason. The existing try/catch still covers the builders.

Residuals belong to the epic final task (task-f3f364a6), not this row:
- On POSIX the terminal's own shell is the user's default profile, which VS Code resolves itself. This row fixes the typed interpreter, as JetBrains does.
- The Accounts sign-in terminal is not a seat launch and stays unchanged.
implementationPlan.note: Added typed protectedInterpreter selecting fixed /bin/bash or SystemRoot System32 PowerShell through installedExecutable. launchRole computes protectedRun with runtimeProfile first, refuses before readiness/terminal, passes accepted interpreter to both builders and win32 shellPath; legacy defaults stay unchanged. New interpreter argument receives C0/DEL validation and native shell quoting. POSIX terminal options and Accounts remain unchanged per residual scope. Fresh two-platform npm test/compile follows in step 4; no production edits preceded step-1 RED.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Under the protected profile (a protected runtime, or a verified-local VM seat), the VS Code seat launch starts the installed wrapper's interpreter by an absolute path outside the workspace:
- POSIX: the real path of /bin/bash, typed as the first word.
- win32: %SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe, used as the terminal's shellPath and typed after `&`.
The path passes installedExecutable's checks, so no PATH or current-directory lookup can select a workspace file. A refused interpreter shows an error and creates no terminal. Legacy launches are byte-identical.
acceptanceCriteria: The protected typed lines and the win32 shellPath name the real absolute interpreter path (L1, V2, V4).
protectedInterpreter refuses a missing, relative or in-project candidate on each platform (L5).
A refusal creates no terminal, and a legacy launch never consults the interpreter check (L6).
Every legacy row and the legacy terminal options are unchanged.
npm test && npm run compile is green in Linux and Windows full-repo snapshots.
invariants: runtimeProfile is called first and exactly once per launch, as today
no sendText or createTerminal on a protected launch without an accepted interpreter
a legacy launch line and its options are byte-identical to HEAD
compatibility: installedExecutable's default label keeps every existing 'node executable' message
the protected rows that pin the old bare-word line (protected-runtime L1, verified-local-launch V2 and V4) are updated by design; no legacy row changes
reuse: MoeDaemonClient.installedExecutable (with a new label parameter) for the outside-the-project and regular-file checks
the protected-runtime.test.cjs harness (loadLauncher, project, extension, declare) for the new rows
sourceAssumptions: moe-vscode/src/util/AgentLauncher.ts:30 WINDOWS_SHELL, :258-288 buildPowerShellCommand, :290-321 buildBashCommand, :351 the protected choice, :411-415 createTerminal
checkRefs: two-leg full-repo snapshot: cd moe-vscode && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm test && npm run compile, run on Linux under env -i and on Windows through cmd.exe, with the four files overlaid (step 4)

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Absolute interpreter in the typed line, plus an absolute win32 shellPath. This mirrors the fix direction of the JetBrains twin task-b071e3bf; a parity note was posted to architect-74d9e1c7 at 08:35Z.

Rejected alternatives:
- A scrubbed PATH through createTerminal's env option: profile rc files can re-add '.', and the typed bare word would still be resolved.
- An absolute POSIX shellPath (/bin/bash) for the terminal itself: zsh users' PATH setup for node and claude lives in .zshrc, so seats would fail with MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND. It is recorded as a residual instead.
- Reimplementing the outside-the-project check: installedExecutable already does it (fully qualified, a regular file by realpath, not a Windows alias, outside the project). It only needs a label parameter.

DoD 2 reading: only the rows that pin the PROTECTED typed line change (protected-runtime L1, verified-local-launch V2 and V4), because DoD 1 changes exactly that line. Every legacy row and the legacy options stay byte-identical.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
AgentLauncher.ts:
- :351 picks the protected runtime when runtimeProfile(...) === 'protected' || vmSeat. runtimeProfile pins, so it must still be called first and exactly once.
- :287 (PowerShell) and :307 (bash) build the typed lines.
- :411-415 creates the terminal; WINDOWS_SHELL ('powershell.exe') is the shellPath on win32 only.

MoeDaemonClient.ts:
- installedExecutable (:582) and selectInstalledFile (:588) hold the protected file checks. defaultFoldCase (:269) and ArtifactSelection (:261) are exported.

Tests:
- They load AgentLauncher in a vm context with an injected client module, so a stubbed installedExecutable can force a refusal on any host.
- windows-terminal-shell.test.cjs simulates win32 on any host, but only for legacy launches. Protected rows must run on their native host, because isFullyQualified and realpath use the real platform.
- moe-agent.sh's shebang is #!/bin/bash.

- MoeDaemonClient.ts is a hot file; keep the label hunk minimal.
